[b]Koroushs Arrival[/b]
[i]Ever since word got out that a coup had occurred in Dhornaper, Hydronian intelligence has been monitoring Dhornaper media. When it was announced that the deposed president Koroush would be exiled to Hydronia, the navy and airforce had been on high alert, looking for where the new government would drop off their former leader. 3 days after the coup took place, a Dhora military vessel was intercepted near a remote port in the state of Turqevia. The ship was allowed to dock and a brief exchange took place. President Koroush was handed over to the Navy and the Dhora ship promptly left and exited Hydronian territorial waters just 38 minutes later. President Koroush was then transported to the main island and driven to Hydropolis, where the president had requested to speak to him[/i]

President Kaplan Zorlu sits in his office on the top floor of the parliamentary office block, awaiting the arrival of Koroush.
[i][b]*knock knock knock*[/i][/b]
[i]Come in![/i]
Koroush enters the office, accompanied by two security officers. The president gestures for them to exit, leaving just him and Koroush. The Dhora speaks first.
[i]Thank you for accepting me into your nation Mr. President, you are clearly aware of my current situation,[/i]
[i]Indeed, youd be surprised how quickly news travels. Im afraid not quick enough however, Im sorry we were not able to take action quicker,[/i]
[i]No need to apologise, it was inevitable[/i]
[i]Anyway, Id like to ask you a few questions to help decide Hydronias course of action.[/i]
[i]of course,[/i]
Koroush proceeds to explain the timeline of events that occurred during the coup. He speaks of how he was notified of the events unfolding in Shar and he was detained by the military and forced to resign. The conversation continues and Koroush makes various recommendations to Zorlu as to what course of action to take.
[i]Thank you Mr. Koroush, this has been very helpful,[/i]
[i]No problem, I only hope you make the best decision[/i]
The president nods in approval as a security officer enters the room to take Koroush to his new home.

Later that day, President Zorlu is notified by the military that satellites above Sal-Baliz also detected movements of Dhora troops along the border with the ULR, a nation that Hydronia shares a good diplomatic relationship with. The president decides to halt all uranium and food shipments to the nation, fearing that they may be used to support the clearly militant new regime

[nation]Dhornaper[/nation]
[nation]Lavinsworth United Islands[/nation]

[nation]Shahzada[/nation] RP

General Fereydun surveys some the build up of his eastern forces in person when he is interrupted by a phone call from the Cabinet Secretary.

"Sir, Hydronia has informed us that they are halting supply of food and uranium to us."

"They're either upset at the coup or the planned military exercises, in either case, they'll get over it eventually. Inform them in turn that aluminium shipments will resume when their shipments resume and that we intend to have friendly relations with Hydronia."

"Yes, sir."

With the conversation over, he turns to his staff. "Get all units built up here in seven days and then immediately put them through hell for three more days. I want them exhausted and spent by the end of the exercises."

[b]From the Sanguinian Herald[/b]

[spoiler=Reconquestus Meridiem]After the costly but successful reconquests of Ottominus and Revinni, the Sanguinian Senate approved a temporary freeze on further expansion, choosing instead to focus on rebuilding those reclaimed cities and reinforcing Ventusias core regions.
Meanwhile, the city of Meridiem, lying just south of Ventusia, remained under de facto control of the Meridiani Provisional Authority  a self-styled independent regime composed of ex-politicians, warlords, and military loyalists who had declared autonomy after the 1999 Ventusian Council.
Though neglected by international diplomacy, Meridiem was secretly armed by black-market actors and foreign-aligned economic factions seeking to prevent Sanguivallis reunification.

In a Cabinet meeting somewhere in June, ministers yelled and argued over each other, each with a cooling cup of coffee. As every minister debated over allocating funds for the upcoming fiscal year, the two front doors busted open.
A staffer rushed through, Clear the room! he shouted, holding a folder, Everyone not on the war council get outNow!
Confused, Abecci asked his Chief of Staff, Whats going on?

Mario Cielinni emerged behind the staffer who urged everyone out, Sir! he cried, placing a folder in front of Abecci. 
Our patrol forces south have been ambushed by Meridiemi forces! 
Abecci began skimming through the document as Cielinni continued, Reports say 4 dead and 15 injured!

Given this, Abecci was infuriated. After weeks of silence from Sanguivallis, carefully rebuilding Ottominus and Revinni.
Curses! I give the immediate order to deploy the 4th Expeditionary Command! he yelled.

Following the border ambush, Consul Abecci gave authorization to resume the expeditionary expansion program, signing a military order labeled Sanguine Spearhead. Within 72 hours, a force of 27,000 troops was assembled under the command of General Sergio Montegna. 

The goal: seize Meridiems central district and neutralize hostile command structures before they could escalate or rally foreign support.

It took half a week to reach the border from Ventusia. They ventured through rivers, creeks, and towns. The locals took notice, waving flags of the serene republic, and handing out bread, water, and portraits of saints to passing men, each man being given good regards. 

By night, the first most regiment reached the old customs checkpoint, not far from the Asylian Mountains, where hidden roadside IEDs detonated, killing 10 and injuring 15. Chaos pouredthe rear, confused, began rushing forward to the customs checkpoint
This is Command Unit Giorno-7! Were under heavy fire near checkpoint M-5ambush confirmed! Repeat, ambush confirmed!

Back in Ventusia, inside the Consular War Room, a live feed relayed battlefield footage, along with a radio.
General Montegna patched in directly.
The radio buzzed in, bullets ricocheting in the back could be heard.
Montegna: "Consul! we are pinned down! Mortar fire, possible foreign arms, we need clearance"
Abecci: "Hold your line, General. Are you receiving return fire?"
Montegna: "Theyre dug in. They shot first, sir. Weve lost 10 already!"
Abecci: "You have full clearance. Return fire and secure your sector.
Montegna: "Understood. Sanguivallis will march south tonight."

The Sanguinian forces made quick work of the ambush.

The next day, Sanguinians marched through mountain passes, as the main road was deemed too dangerous due to lingering enemy snipers. With brief skirmishes and harassments here and there, the city of Meridiem slowly came into view.

Meridiem was situated by the foothills of the Asylian Mountains. It controlled the only way, the only pass to Oceanium. Meridiem forces were estimated to have a combined strength of 9,500 men strong. A mix of irregular militia, foreign armed radicals, and ex-military, complete with superior knowledge regarding the terrain. Intelligence forces say that Meridiemi militia equipped themselves with smuggled arms from foreign enterprises.

Over the next 48 hours, the outskirts of Meridiem were bombarded with prayers, peace terms, and patriotic music. Sanguinian airforce vehicles airdropped pamphlets into the city, urging the local populace to rise up against the provisional regime.

Despite this, hardliners in the Mountain Republic refused negotiations.

Sanguinian forces pushed forward  clearing pillboxes, torching illegal radio towers, and flushing out sniper nests with controlled demolitions. Combat became brutal as the full Expeditionary force closed in. East of the city in particular, guerrilla forces ambushed combat vehicles from treetop perches.

[b]The High Church Massacre[/b]

At Meridiems abandoned High Church, once a Catholic symbol before being repurposed by the Mountain Republic as a barracks, a squad of Sanguinian scouts were captured and executed by hanging from the bell tower. Their bodies were left as a warning.
General Montegna ordered the first airstrike of the campaign.
Three precision drone-guided bombs cratered the central square, leveling the makeshift barracks. That act shattered public confidence in the regime  and began the desertion of local militia.

The campaign froze. General Montegna, not willing to risk utter destruction of the city, called for a siege. It was a very endearing move, a very risky choice, the strategy now was to starve the city. Montegnas reason as to not have assaulted was due to the policy of taking the city, not destroying it. Other than that, urban warfare was risky, as there were no given insider knowledge regarding the citys layout. Nevertheless, airstrike after airstrike were called only on military installments.

Ten days into the siege, a group of defectors emerged from the mountains under white cloth, waving relics of Sanguivallisold crimson banners, worn medallions, berets from the time of the 4 great fathers. They called themselves the Sons of the Valley, a secret loyalist brotherhood hiding in Meridiem since 1999, surviving purges and authoritarian rule.
Their leader gave crucial He brought with him old Meridiem sewer schematics, entrances to ancient overlooked city aqueducts, knowledge of a fuel depot turned barracks in the west quarter, and rotations of Meridiems night patrols.

Still under suspicion, General Montegna sent them to Ventusia, where they met the consul himself. After some time, a new plan was drawn.

Using the defectors intelligence, General Montegna split the siege into three coordinated operations:
1. Operazione Monaciello
A diversionary frontal assault on the southern gate, using reserve units and dummy mortars. 
Objective: force defenders to concentrate on the front.
2. Operazione Borda
The 4th Expeditionary Command, under the cover of night, entered the sewer system through three old tunnels detailed by the Sons of the Valley. 
Objective: emerge in the central plaza behind enemy lines.
3. Operazione Martello di Ferro
A small mechanized detachment would strike the western depot during Monaciellos peak. If successful, it would cut off fuel, ammunition, and emergency routes.
The hours were gruelling. Man after man fell side by side. On the Meridiemi side, men scattered like bugs due to the occasional airstrikes from the Sanguinian side. 

The plan succeedednot without blood.
Monaciello saw brutal pushback; 600 Sanguinians wounded, 87 dead.

Bordas tunnel teams emerged and seized the plaza bell tower, raising the Sanguinian flagvisible from the southern ridgeline.

Martello di Ferros mechanized unit managed to destroy the depot in a surprise blitzkrieg, crippling the defenders.

By dawn, half of Meridiem had fallen.
 The rest laid down their arms within 36 hours.

[b]Post Conquest.[/b]

The provisional government, led by acting mayor Giulio Marfenna, fled the city under nightfall through back roads into the Montes Custodii. Intelligence suggests some officials may have escaped across borders, but most have either been captured or are now fugitives.
Several extremist holdouts attempted a last-stand barricade within Meridiems historical archives near the eastern quarter, planting booby traps and invoking slogans from defunct revolutionary sects. After a brief skirmish, the Reggimento Specializzato di Alpinismo, subdued the radicals and arrested their leaders, some of whom were masked figures tied to the old separatist-era militias from the early 2000s.

[b]A Rosary in the Square[/b]

On the morning after the citys fall, General Montegna organized a public rosary in the city square, once the site of revolutionary rallies and book burnings. It was to be presided over by a priest from Ventusia.
Over 400 civilians gathered  some out of faith, others out of fatigue, some just watching silently as the decades-old crucifix from the Meridiem convent was lifted back onto its old post.
Sanguinian troops formed a wide cordon as the final Gloria Patri echoed through the square.
Population Control

The urban districts were immediately placed under temporary martial supervision. Sanguinian troops:
-Imposed a 5:00 p.m. curfew.
-Collected and catalogued thousands of unlicensed weapons;
-Cleared roads and reconnected power stations and radio towers.
To calm the populace, local broadcasts reassured residents they would not be subject to forced conscription or seizure of homes, and that aid rations would be distributed evenly in the following days. Public info centers were opened in Meridiems train depot and three community centers to re-register citizens into the Sanguinian census system.
Abeccis office also announced an amnesty clause for former Meridiemi civil servants and police officers willing to cooperate with investigators.

[b]Back in Ventusia[/b]

In the capital, the War Cabinet met in the Consuls chambers, where Mario Cielinni, Chief of Staff, read aloud the final communiqué from General Montegna.
"Meridiem is under full control. The Sons of the Valley are safe. Radical cells have been dismantled. The city is quiet, and her people are watching us."
As silence fell, Consul Abecci stood up and raised a glass.
"To Meridiem," he said. "To the men we sent, the sons who returned, and the people who held the memory of our flag through dark decades."
The Cabinet toasted. Across Ventusia, fireworks erupted in small plazas, radios blared national hymns, and for a moment, the war-weary republic allowed itself to breathe.

[i]The sun casted its glow over Meridiem.

High was the flag of the Serene Republic, raised by men of the military.

Men, Women, and Children took to the streets and sang:

We slept beneath the chestnut tree,

 With stars behind our backs.

 The wind it sang so patiently,

 Of love and far-off tracks.
My fathers coat, my mothers ring,

 I wear them every mile.

 And when the fig trees bloom in spring,

 I see their laughing smiles.
Oh Sanguivallis, land of red,

 Where rivers cut the plain

 You hold our names when we are gone,

 And call us home again.
If I should fall on foreign land,

 Let not my name be lost.

 Bury me near the vineyard stone,

 And light a flame at dusk.[/i][/spoiler]
